reviews.text: Davis Guggenheim’s luminous, eye-opening documentary Still: A Michael J. Fox Movie gives us a never-before-seen look into the life of one of Hollywood’s most loved stars.
reviews.author: William Stottor

reviews.text: When dealing with the actor’s exciting film-world or the sad reality of his diagnosis, Still: A Michael J. Fox Movie never loses that special spark, the actor’s very own.
reviews.author: Diana Tuova

reviews.text: Davis Guggenheim strikes up a conversation with the Family Ties actor who does not hold any reservations while delving into his career choices, personal life, and activism.
reviews.author: Tamma Moksha

reviews.text: Fox is interviewed extensively in this movie, and he is funny, disarming and upbeat. He always has a quip ready for any occasion. It is easy to see the personality and wit that made him so popular, even in the advanced stages of his illness.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: Guggenheim makes it clear from the very beginning of this clear-eyed, honest, and cleverly edited Apple TV+ film that he understands the through-lines in Fox’s life.
reviews.author: Jen Chaney

reviews.text: An extraordinarily intimate portrait of the actor who used a diagnosis of Parkinson’s to discover he is really was and what he could do for the world.
reviews.author: Frederic and Mary Ann Brussat

reviews.text: Poignant and powerful. Still skillfully weaves together humor and nostalgia using archival footage, scripted recreations, and a personal interview with Michael J. Fox.
reviews.author: Mark Johnson

reviews.text: Fox is an inspirational, courageous warrior, and a selfless humanitarian of the highest order. God bless him, his family, and the millions of other Parkinson’s patients and their families the world over.
reviews.author: Michael Clark

reviews.text: This hero is unstoppable, he will crack a wry joke, and make a hard-earned pronouncement even as he fights to operate his body....buoyed by that deep optimism that made him sparkle all these years. It is a phenomenal gift to us.
reviews.author: Anne Brodie

reviews.text: Still is inspiring without trying because of Fox’s openness and genuine personality. He’s still the funny, fierce, and easy-going guy he always was. Watching him isn't heartbreaking but rather endearing and uplifting.
reviews.author: Akos Peterbencze

reviews.text: If Fox's Parkinson's is well-known, after opening the documentary with it, what follows is a sort of narrated biography. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: Still really uses its subject’s vast history of recorded entertainment and archival footage to create a sweeping testament and tribute to Fox.
reviews.author: Glenn Dunks

reviews.text: Still is a nuanced meditation on the price of success.
reviews.author: Henry K. Miller

reviews.text: There’s warmth and ease with how director Davis Guggenheim and Michael J. Fox tell his story. Michael admits that he wants to capture his life before he’s no longer to share it.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: While Fox may be petrified of Parkinson’s overtaking him, he rarely lets you see it. Whether it’s making it from one point to the next with his physical therapist or simply walking on a beach with his family, Fox just keeps going.
reviews.author: Dan Buffa

reviews.text: For every sobering moment in this sometimes difficult but ultimately life-affirming documentary, Fox turns hopelessness on its head, wringing joy from every fleeting victory; laughing uproariously with the love of his life..and grown kids who adore him.
reviews.author: Bill Newcott

reviews.text: Still: A Michael J. Fox Movie is a marvel on many levels, starting with the short kid who became a superstar and ending with an honest and grateful man who cannot hold still.
reviews.author: Martha K. Baker

reviews.text: Fox’s quick wit illuminates this remarkable documentary … The effect is uncannily vivid and playful, like being in the passenger seat of the time-travelling DeLorean.
reviews.author: Mel Campbell

reviews.text: The film also uses scenes from Fox's own films and TV shows to illustrate points Fox makes about his life. It might inject unintended meaning into some of the footage, but it makes for compelling visual storytelling.
reviews.author: Jennifer Green

reviews.text: It’s a cozy profile that invites empathy more than sympathy.
reviews.author: Rob Gonsalves

reviews.text: Still isn’t about fame, or illness, but instead the strength of character it takes to navigate both. “I’m a tough son of a bitch” Fox declares early on, and Guggenheim’s triumphant film only cements that claim.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: Still is a documentary that not only situates itself in nostalgia, but it is also a film that shows us what living with Parkinson's is like [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alejandro Alemán

reviews.text: You can’t help but empathize with Fox as you watch Still, but this is no pity party — it’s a celebration of a life well lived, even if that living hasn’t always been something out of the movies or TV.
reviews.author: Mark Meszoros

reviews.text: Michael J. Fox is a survivor and  an inspiration despite the world swirling around him.  The same person who worked days shooting Family Ties and evenings at Back to the Future - doesn't know what giving up is and thank goodness for us he never will.
reviews.author: Carla Renata

reviews.text: ... This documentary does not resort to cheap shots or sentimentality, instead, it uses the troublesome experience in an artistic way. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Emiliano Basile

reviews.text: Still doesn’t sugarcoat what Fox is facing these days, but it nevertheless strikes a tone of positivity.
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: Asked why he wants to continue to tell his story, he says, “I love my mind and I love the places it takes me and I just don’t want that to get cut short.” Anyone who watches this uplifting film will share that feeling.
reviews.author: Stephen Romei

reviews.text: Still [is] like watching Fox’s life back through a new filter...
reviews.author: Larushka Ivan-Zadeh

reviews.text: Of the 30 films I screened at Sundance Film Festival, this was my number 1 choice--an excellent biography with themes of love, persistence, addiction, optimism and hope are a true testament to overcoming adversity.
reviews.author: Sarah Knight Adamson

reviews.text: While gimmicky at times, the film offers some poignant glimpses of the star’s Parkinson’s symptoms and his 1.21-gigawatt personality.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: This is a wonderful movie.
reviews.author: Andy Klein

reviews.text: Absolutely terrific. It is both heartbreaking and inspiring at the same time, and I think that's by design.
reviews.author: Wade Major

reviews.text: It’s hard not to like Fox, and the film only deepens that by detailing what he’s overcome, his acceptance of his current challenges and commitment to family.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: This is an interesting look into the life of an inspiring person.
reviews.author: Jeremy Jahns

reviews.text: Outstanding...Thankfully, Fox adopts a distinct pity-me-not attitude.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: Assembled warmly and unflinchingly, this documentary is a powerfully moving portrait of the actor who charmed the world in the 1980s and 1990s and has lived with Parkinson's for three decades.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: Still: A Michael J. Fox Movie is more than a classic story of overcoming adversity; it transmits an inspiring message about appreciating life as an experience filled with lights and shadows... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Loser

reviews.text: The unforgettable documentary demonstrates realism and emotion, while never going too far down the rabbit hole of sadness, finding the light in Fox’s life as well.
reviews.author: Tarek Fayoumi

reviews.text: For me, the title suggests something else, he's still here -- living as fully as he can and offering a story that's sure to inspire others.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: A reminder of Fox's greatness as an entertainer and a human being. Love this guy.
reviews.author: Bob Grimm

reviews.text: “Still” focuses deftly not just on how Fox’s world evolved in the wake of his Parkinson’s diagnosis in the 1990s, but on how Fox now sees his entire existence when filtered through what he’s survived, what he’s celebrated, and what he’s won and lost.
reviews.author: Matthew Jackson

reviews.text: STILL is an impressive, inspiring and sometimes heartbreaking look at Fox’s ongoing journey, made all the more powerful for being told in his voice.
reviews.author: Tara Bennett

reviews.text: Guggenheim flexes both muscles in telling a profile on someone and using his directorial skills. It’s one of the best documentaries of 2023.
reviews.author: Leo Brady

reviews.text: While the material itself is straightforwardly biographical, the presentation is imaginative, making “Still” engaging for its style as well as its content.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: Beneath its fizzy clips and Eighties pop soundtrack, Guggenheim’s film sometimes has the soft contours of a standard showbusiness autobiography, with Oedipal tussles, twinkling ironies and lucky breaks...
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: The filmmakers don't try to dwell on the sadness. It's one of those documentaries that puts life into perspective.
reviews.author: Korey Coleman

reviews.text: Still is an entertaining and unique documentary that reveals the early life of the star Michael J. Fox, how he became famous, and, in a sort of way, reintroduces him to those who grew up with him.
reviews.author: Sarah Ksiazek

reviews.text: Inspiring and with superb film editing, Still: A Michael J. Fox Movie is a must-see documentary for anyone who wants to get a personal look at how Michael J. Fox refused to make his Parkinson's disease into a tragedy but instead turned it into a triumph.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: The documentary is both heartbreaking and uplifting, told in a captivating narrative to showcase how despite a debilitating disease, Michael J Fox is thriving and triumphant.
reviews.author: Chris Joyce

reviews.text: Neither a pity party nor a puff piece, the film is a thoughtful chronicle of the life and career of one-time “Boy Prince” of Hollywood as told through his performances and candid conversations with the film’s director Davis Guggenheim.
reviews.author: Lynn Venhaus

reviews.text: A dazzling collage of interviews, dramatisations, snappily chosen film and TV clips, family footage and narrated biography...
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: Tmphatically captures that vivid, peculiar energy that has always been present in the 1980s-bred star’s performances: restlessness coupled with a bracing agitation... Funny, heartfelt, sometimes harrowing, and whiz-bang entertaining.
reviews.author: Ray Pride

reviews.text: Still: A Michael J. Fox Movie is a documentary in constant motion, and just like the older Fox, it knows when to stop, pause and take it all in.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: Guggenheim’s documentary employs clever editing, using Michael Fox’s onscreen fictional characters to illustrate his biography and his transition from '80s’ hot-shot star to a still funny but thoughtful advocate for Parkinson’s disease.
reviews.author: Liam Lacey

reviews.text: What was particular effective is when director Guggenheim, with his editor Michael Harte, intercut the clip history to create the MJF man in motion. This creative approach gives Fox the story and recognition that he deserves. With director interview.
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: The falls and significant breaks/bruises that come with it are all part of a great personal story based on Fox's four books and filled with more hope and humor than sadness and suffering. Blessings and good thoughts all around.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: If Still: A Michael J. Fox Movie shows us anything, it’s the extinguishable spirit and lust for life that has kept this man going for decades. He’s unstoppable on so many fronts and remains a stunning encouragement and role model for many.
reviews.author: Tynan Yanaga

reviews.text: 'Still' is a moving document and a reminder why Michael J. Fox always enjoys an invitation into our living rooms and movie theatres.  Prepare for admiration, laughter, and tears.
reviews.author: Jeff Mitchell

reviews.text: This endlessly inventive, entertaining, enlightening and yes, emotional documentary [is] one of the year’s must-see movies.
reviews.author: James Croot

reviews.text: Like the best of its kind, the film reminds the rest of us that there's often a gulf between our perception of the challenges we face in this world and their actual size.
reviews.author: Harry Guerin

reviews.text: It gives us some of what we want – nostalgia, an inside look at a famous person’s life. But it gives us a lot of what we need – honesty and truth.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: This captivating documentary digs beneath the typical celebrity retrospective while examining Fox's career and his resilience.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: The best parts of "Still" strip away the artifice and let Fox speak for himself.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: In the film, Guggenheim both presents Fox as he is today, hampered but not imprisoned by the ravages of illness, and as he was in yesteryear, courtesy of generous sampling of his many performances.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: But this film is about much more than Parkinson's. It's also about the preciousness of a close family and the peculiarity of becoming a movie star.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: The heart and soul of the film are the face-to-face interviews, which are far less delicate than one might expect. And all the deeper for it.
reviews.author: John Anderson

reviews.text: There are life lessons here to be learned and shared, for sure. But the film moves with such thrilling pacing it feels more like a celebration.
reviews.author: Christy Lemire

reviews.text: In terms of serving as a source of inspiration in terms of dealing with the bad hand that he was dealt, this “Michael J. Fox Movie” makes him look 10-feet tall.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: A great double-feature title to go alongside INTRODUCING, SELMA BLAIR: candid looks inside diseases as told by charismatic entertainers who can no longer be quite who they once were that prove powerful documents of humanity's perseverance.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: Simultaneously heartbreaking and inspirational, the film provides an unvarnished look at Fox’s daily struggles as well as the small triumphs that provide an illusionary respite from his trial.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: It’s shocking but inspiring. Parkinson’s hasn’t robbed Fox of his drive or his sense of humour.
reviews.author: Andy Lea

reviews.text: The icon reflects on his career in Still: A Michael J. Fox Movie while showing the difficult life he lives. This behind-the-scenes view of his life and career highlights the importance of his activism for the past twenty-five years.
reviews.author: Alan French

reviews.text: How we handle the cards we’re dealt is everything, and Davis Guggenheim’s remarkable documentary Still: A Michael J. Fox Movie reminds us that a person stricken with a disease doesn’t become that disease.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: The beats of stardom are interesting, if not surprising.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: Watching this movie, you remember that funny, needling, nervy little guy up on the screen, and you realize you’re rooting for him. Still.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: While Still: A Michael J Fox Movie is never less than an engaging watch, you'll wish it ended up digging into more of Fox's life in the way a documentary usually would.
reviews.author: Ian Sandwell

reviews.text: It's a respectful film about a man wholly worthy of that respect.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: Even though the fresh material is limited, the documentary leaves us with a more genuine portrait of the actor.
reviews.author: Jorge Ignacio Castillo

reviews.text: It's a testament to a performer who refuses to meet life's curveballs with anything less than grace and good humour. And STILL is a fitting tribute, told with cinematic craft and care.
reviews.author: Luke Goodsell

reviews.text: Essentially, the monologues are great, but it’s the back and forth (including the banter between Fox and his delightfully unglossy family) that makes Still unmissable.
reviews.author: Charlotte O'Sullivan

reviews.text: This is all solid, determinedly upbeat stuff – a tale of perseverance rather than of hardship.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: Still is a classy mixture of nostalgia, celebrity and hope that is sure to move you.
reviews.author: Grant Rollings

reviews.text: Stirring stuff.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: Sets itself apart from the glut of streaming documentaries by taking a cinematic approach, rather than resembling a glorified newsmagazine episode.
reviews.author: Josh Bell

reviews.text: What stands out in “Still: A Michael J. Fox Movie” is the candor and determination of its subject.
reviews.author: Odie Henderson

reviews.text: Movies about illness are so often vehicles for easy sentiment: isn’t he or she brave, or thank god I am not like that. This one is funny, full of sharp insight and unusually frank language. It’s also doggedly unsentimental.
reviews.author: Paul Byrnes

reviews.text: By turns heartwarming and heartbreaking, this is a fascinating and funny twin portrait of a Hollywood rise-and-fall, and the realities of living with Parkinson’s.
reviews.author: John Nugent

reviews.text: Fox seems every bit a guy we’d all like if we met him, but it seems like hagiography all the same.
reviews.author: Leslie Felperin

reviews.text: With apologies to Dr. Emmett Brown, you don’t need a flux capacitor to build a time machine. All you need to do is make a film.
reviews.author: Ben Kenigsberg

reviews.text: Fox is such an engaging, honest, and frankly funny narrator of his own life that "Still” is lively and entertaining when it could be despairing. We always feel for Fox. But we never feel sorry for him.
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: It’s a revealing documentary about a man who was once one of the busiest actors in Hollywood who has learned in transition to appreciate the loved ones around him even more.
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: As rote as many celebrity navel-gazing documentaries have become, it’s refreshing to see a film that can still find the strengths of the format.
reviews.author: Leigh Monson

reviews.text: The story of a plucky kid who rises, falls a little and then gets back up to face another day. And if that sounds like a typical Michael J. Fox movie to you, well, you’re not far off.
reviews.author: Michael J. Casey

reviews.text: Still paints a complete picture of Fox the man, someone who’s been to the height of fame and brought low by a disease that can be managed but not cured.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: 'Still' is equal parts heartbreaking and hopeful.
reviews.author: Murjani Rawls

reviews.text: The result is a biographical documentary that frames the actor’s life as a feel-good story in the first half and a taut psychological drama in the second.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: Simultaneously raw and delicate, tough and fun, emotional and intelligent. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: Michael J. Fox makes clear that he does not want anyone to throw him a pity party. Watching Guggenheim's well-crafted film shows how this consummate entertainer continues to defy the odds, leading a full life, acting and STILL going strong.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: Guggenheim and Fox paint a portrait of a talented guy overcoming multiple hurdles by coming to grips with the left field blow of an incurable medical diagnosis usually reserved for those in their senior years.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: The still charismatic and gregarious Fox is able to captivate the viewer through the simple act of running back the clock and not having to worry about killing the image he once had as an actor.
reviews.author: Andrew Parker

reviews.text: ... "Still: A Michael J. Fox Movie" gives the audience everything Guggenheim intends: a warm tribute to a career beloved by many without losing sight of the person audiences attached onto.
reviews.author: Douglas Davidson

reviews.text: 'Still' is not about an actor brought low by a medical condition, a redemption story, or even his resilience in the face of it all. 'Still' goes much deeper than that, and talks about how a person can spend their lives trying to run away from themselves.
reviews.author: Brian Lloyd

reviews.text: A moving, funny, and illuminating film.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: Michael J. Fox hasn’t given up yet. He still has an immensely likable and funny on-camera persona, and now he is using that gift to share hope, joy and perhaps a sense of acceptance with others.
reviews.author: Michael O'Sullivan

reviews.text: As for those too young to remember the era that Fox defined, this film will introduce them to an indomitable spirit who manages to locate humour in confronting the hand he’s been dealt.
reviews.author: Hilary A White

reviews.text: A remarkable portrait of a remarkable life.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: All of this is interesting, in varying degrees. But watching and listening to Fox talk is magnetic.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: [A]  glossy, entertaining and often affecting documentary.
reviews.author: Jake Coyle

reviews.text: It presents a raw, unfiltered look at Fox, who in the years since his diagnosis, has raised over $2 billion dollars for Parkinson research as well as raising three children and maintaining a steady acting career.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: An honest, intimate, and heartbreaking portrait; The story of a great man, who will not stop fighting to enjoy his life and his family until the last possible second. [Full Review in Spanish}
reviews.author: Laura Hiros

reviews.text: Its best, [when] it backs off and lets Fox’s presence, the grace-filled and inspiring way he has risen to an extremely tough occasion, reflect the man’s lives and times.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: STILL: A Michael J. Fox Movie is an intimate look at his life and career through his own words. It's an honest, raw, and emotional exploration of an actor at the high of his career and how Parkinson's changed all of that in an instant.
reviews.author: Matt Rodriguez

reviews.text: A well-crafted look at Michael J. Fox that balances affectionate nostalgia with unflinching candour.
reviews.author: Neil Smith

reviews.text: Although Still takes audiences on an emotional ride, it’s an upbeat tale true to the spirit of its subject. The film casts Fox as the underdog in his own story.
reviews.author: Pat Mullen

reviews.text: There’s an enviable mix of the playful and the poignant.
reviews.author: Amber Wilkinson

reviews.text: The film is eminently engaging and impactful in its exploration of Fox’s journey and his overall message of hopefulness...
reviews.author: Josh Flanders

reviews.text: If anyone ever thinks of Michael J. Fox as anything other than a legend after this film, they need to re-evaluate their priorities. Still: A Michael J. Fox Movie documents the life of a survivor, who is far from done fighting.
reviews.author: Martin Carr

reviews.text: A lovingly edited portrait using Fox's words, his voice and his image to tell the story of a life well lived
reviews.author: Erik Childress

reviews.text: A bittersweet and inspiring story of a bright light and his life well-lived.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: STILL is an exercise in Fox taking the reins on his own story, and I wish I could have heard more, especially about how he still sometimes acts in guest shots on various television series.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: The final result is more for the no doubt multitude of fans who will be satisfied by a casual perusal of one of most recognizable and enjoyable celebrities, but there’s little to recommend beyond the usual fluff piece.
reviews.author: Andrea Thompson

reviews.text: A film about a beloved performer struggling with a devastating degenerative illness probably has no business being as funny and entertaining as this one.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: [Still is] not subtle in the delivery of its message, but it is also quite obvious that this is entirely by design, the story of a man who may have physically changed but has not allowed this debilitating disease to dampen his enthusiasm for life.
reviews.author: Steven Warner

reviews.text: The craft of the documentary goes beyond a formal interview, with a presentation style that had to be meticulously planned to work as effectively as it does here.
reviews.author: Amy Smith

reviews.text: A great testament to what making lemonade from life’s lemons can do for one’s soul.
reviews.author: Nick Johnston

reviews.text: It’s a deeply profound meditation on the life and career of one of America’s most beloved actors.
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: A raw and powerful look at one of our most beloved actors. Never failing to bring humor and inspiration, Michael J. Fox’s journey is a recipe for one of the year’s most fascinating documentaries.
reviews.author: David Gonzalez

reviews.text: I wish that his early life could have been told more simply without those ironised faux-biog clips, but this is a highly watchable and affecting film.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: Still is a deserving, well-crafted tale of a remarkable individual, one whose charm remains unabated.
reviews.author: Jason Gorber

reviews.text: A great example of documentary filmmaking that doesn't repeat the same tired format or troupes of other films of the same ilk.
reviews.author: Rachel Ho

reviews.text: Still: A Michael J. Fox Movie is a frank, funny, and moving look at a beloved actor.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: blends biographical documentary style and narrative storytelling to paint a portrait of an extraordinary man.
reviews.author: Raquel Stecher

reviews.text: Boring is a word that never applies to Still: A Michael J. Fox Movie, the captivating interview-based documentary, amplified by re-enactments and endless stock footage and archival material.
reviews.author: Richard Whittaker

reviews.text: An insightful, creatively edited documentary from director Davis Guggenheim that makes good on its title.
reviews.author: Jake Kring-Schreifels

reviews.text: "With Fox’s help, Guggenheim creates a compelling if perhaps unintentional narrative about the way disabled people are forced to contort themselves into a world that doesn’t accommodate them — and the possibilities that open up for them when it does."
reviews.author: Cate Young

reviews.text: A work of empowerment and empathy, a celebration of Fox’s life as an actor and philanthropist.
reviews.author: Tomris Laffly

reviews.text: The Beloved Actor Gets An Uplifting, Entertaining And Truly Cinematic Documentary.
reviews.author: Ethan Anderton

reviews.text: Film showcases the wit and determination of Fox who constantly proves he is the same person that became so popular in the 1980s. It is not about how Parkinson’s disease changed Fox’s life, but is just a part of his larger story.
reviews.author: Nathaniel Muir

reviews.text: Its poignancy and humor is amplified by its canny decision to let Fox tell his own tale.
reviews.author: Nick Schager

reviews.text: Guggenheim and his subject also want to show what it’s like to be Michael J. Fox right now, and that’s really where this documentary... turns into something else entirely -- something beyond praise or tragedy.
reviews.author: David Fear

reviews.text: Still: A Michael J. Fox Movie can be a bit standard as far as biographical documentaries go, but when the subject is someone as much to watch as Fox is, it’s hard to care too much about the form when the content is so captivating.
reviews.author: Ross Bonaime

reviews.text: This is a vulnerable and triumphant portrayal of a man who has continued to persevere in the midst of an illness that has threatened his life and his legacy.  It is a stunning technical achievement in documentary filmmaking.
reviews.author: Ty Cooper

reviews.text: Still: A Michael J. Fox Movie is a charming, moving, concisely crafted docu-profile that’ll be easy catnip for Fox’s fans, all while avoiding frothy sentimentality.
reviews.author: Shaun Munro

reviews.text: Incredibly candid but told with warmth and humour. Similar to Fox’s stance on life, it never seeks to elicit sadness or pity. Instead it is a celebration of an amazing talent on screen and inspiration off it.
reviews.author: Dallas King

reviews.text: Anyone who’s had a family member or friend with Parkinson’s will watch this film agog that Fox is even still alive at this point, that his family still has a sense of humor and that they’re not all drinking. Living with Parkinson’s is no sitcom.
reviews.author: Roger Friedman

reviews.text: That is the Michael that the film shows us: someone who to this day continues to fight Parkinson's disease, personally and through a foundation. But it also makes us feel something for him; not pity, but admiration. Full review in Spanish.
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: STILL: A Michael J. Fox Movie is one of the best documentaries of the year.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: There’s undeniable emotional power coursing through every frame [of Still: A Michael J. Fox Movie].
reviews.author: Brian Tallerico

reviews.text: While Fox's most debilitating symptoms engender sympathy, the film astutely avoids pity. Fox himself convinces the viewer to accept and support him without any such condescending judgments while the film presents him in a compatible format.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: Guggenheim based his film on the memoirs of Fox, and with Fox on camera has stunningly created a new memoir that is just as vital and entertaining and enlightening as yes, A Michael J. Fox Movie.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: Through “Still,” Fox lets audiences see him as he is now. He’s smaller than many realize, and that’s another source of self-deprecating humor. But allowing his disability to be shown is a kind of strength.
reviews.author: Peter Debruge

reviews.text: Fox is nothing if not a likable figure, and he and Guggenheim have crafted a likable film about both his suffering and resilience without turning him into a martyr.
reviews.author: Esther Zuckerman

reviews.text: Admirable and intimate...
reviews.author: Daniel Fienberg

reviews.text: A compelling, heartfelt tribute to an inspiring icon.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

synopsis: The film, which will incorporate documentary, archival and scripted elements, will recount Fox's extraordinary story in his own words -- the improbable tale of an undersized kid from a Canadian army base who rose to the heights of stardom in 1980s Hollywood. The account of Fox's public life, full of nostalgic thrills and cinematic gloss, will unspool alongside his never-before-seen private journey, including the years that followed his diagnosis, at 29, with Parkinson's disease. Intimate and honest, and produced with unprecedented access to Fox and his family, the film will chronicle Fox's personal and professional triumphs and travails, and will explore what happens when an incurable optimist confronts an incurable disease. With a mix of adventure and romance, comedy and drama, watching the film will feel like... well, like a Michael J. Fox movie.
